quote: one thing I'm a little concerned about is you've got some trees that are putting some shade on the home.
stewart_read: Rep opens with a disqualifying frame instead of curiosity or qualification. This primes the whole call toward exit rather than toward building interest in seeing a design.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may have been trying to get ahead of a hard DQ efficiently rather than waste time, but she does this before even asking the interest question or capturing the bill — premature.
coaching_implication: Coach to complete verify (interest reason, bill, roof) before raising shading concerns, so any DQ decision is made with full context, not on the first data point.

quote: the highest bill I've ever had was a $109. And my average bill, I'd say, over a course of twelve months is around 76 to $81.
stewart_read: Customer volunteers detailed bill figures unprompted — a rare gift of real usage data. Rep never acknowledges or reflects the number back, flipped or otherwise.
coaching_implication: This is the single biggest missed anchor on the call. Even with a low bill, the rep could have used the number to keep the design conversation open ('at $80 you may not save much, but let's see what the numbers actually show') rather than let it pass unaddressed.

quote: I've dealt with solar, like, quite a bit. So I don't I don't I mean, regardless of their incentives or not, it's just I don't think it can be done. But, I mean, I'm more willing to listen.
stewart_read: Customer discloses significant prior solar experience/quotes ('breakeven over twenty one years... used to be a thirty six year payback') and explicit openness to continue. Rep never asks who he talked to, what was quoted, or what changed his numbers — competitive intel left on the table.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may have judged the shading issue as disqualifying regardless of prior quotes, making the probe moot — but this is undercut by the customer's own line that he's 'more willing to listen,' which the rep talks past.
coaching_implication: Coach to ask a follow-up like 'who ran those numbers for you before?' — this is free competitive intelligence for the closer even if the call doesn't book.

quote: I think where where the situation is, where I'm at, right, is your home doesn't get enough sun exposure for a system to even work effectively.
stewart_read: Rep makes a technical design determination (sun exposure sufficiency) that belongs to the design/closer team using satellite and shading tools, not a setter's phone judgment.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep could be applying a known hard-DQ heuristic from training (heavy shade = don't bother), but nothing in the transcript shows she checked imagery or a shading tool before asserting this as fact.
coaching_implication: Coach the universal escape hatch: 'Let me have our design team pull satellite imagery and see what the shading actually looks like' instead of self-diagnosing and closing the lead on the call.

quote: yeah, like you said, you're not open to removing the trees at all, so solar won't work for you. I can just remove you from my list.
stewart_read: This is a cost/feasibility objection wrapped in a tree-shade objection. Rather than reframe or route to design review, the rep accepts the objection at face value and offers to disqualify — the opposite of the inversion the schema calls for.
alternative_hypothesis: The tree may in fact be a hard technical blocker making inversion moot — but the rep has not verified this with any tool, so treating it as settled fact is premature, not confirmed.
coaching_implication: Replay this line with the rep: the closing move should be 'let's still get a design pulled so you can see exactly what output looks like with the shading — no obligation,' not immediate list removal.

quote: I'll put that here. If things change, you know, if you ever wanna look at options, feel free to give me a call.
stewart_read: Call ends with a passive, customer-initiated-only re-engagement path and no rep-owned next step, callback time, or even a note that the lead will be revisited.
coaching_implication: Even on a probable DQ, the rep should own a next step — e.g., 'I'll flag this for our design team to double check the shading and follow up with you in two weeks' — rather than leaving it entirely on the customer to call back.
